page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation. The memory configuration consists of 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 136.6 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 23.42 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, while complex workloads like software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations score in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated AMD EPYC execution without massive memory overhead. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the lack of local storage, this instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic web serving, text processing, or small-scale LLM inference text generation where high memory capacity is not required. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, parallelized compilation, or heavy multi-threaded processing.
